headline_marked: [[Goalless first half in Messi's final match]] for Argentina against Benin in Buenos Aires
headline: Goalless first half in Messi's final match for Argentina against Benin in Buenos Aires
summary: The legendary Argentine superstar took the field for the last time in the sky-blue and white jersey against Benin at Estadio Monumental. Despite several attacks, neither team managed to score in the first half.
details: In an international friendly, Argentina and Benin concluded the first half in a goalless draw. The match, held on Wednesday (October 6) at Buenos Aires' iconic Estadio Monumental, marked Lionel Messi's final appearance in the sky-blue and white jersey for his country.

From the outset, the hosts dominated ball possession, putting Benin's defense under considerable pressure. However, Argentina's forward line, including Messi, struggled to find the back of the net despite several attempts.

A poignant moment occurred just 10 minutes into the game when the referee paused play for about a minute and a half to honor 'LM10'. Spectators in the stadium rose, applauding and chanting 'Ole Ole Messi' to salute the superstar.

Play resumed, but neither team scored before the break. While the score remained 0-0, the match's primary draw was Messi himself. In the first half, Leo touched the ball in Benin's box 6 times and took a maximum of 4 shots, with billions of fans worldwide eagerly awaiting his magic in the second half.

headline: Ronaldo accuses Portugal coach Jesus of breaking promises, explains camp exit
summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has accused Portugal coach Jorge Jesus of twice breaking his word, leading to his departure from the national team camp. Despite the dispute, Ronaldo insists he remains available for selection after any potential punishment.
details: Cristiano Ronaldo has publicly accused Portugal coach Jorge Jesus of twice breaking his word, detailing the dispute that led to his departure from the national team camp last week. The 41-year-old forward provided his account in a lengthy statement.

Ronaldo stated that Jesus had initially agreed he would miss the Norway and Denmark matches to manage his fitness. However, on the day of the Norway game, the coach informed him he would play for 30 minutes.

Despite warming up from halftime onwards, Ronaldo was not called upon to play. He described watching the minutes tick by without being brought into the game, which contradicted their prior understanding.

A subsequent meeting with Jesus, attended by Al Nassr's sporting director, resulted in an agreement for the coach to clarify events at his next press conference. An eight-point document was prepared, stating Ronaldo never demanded playing time and respected decisions.

Ronaldo claims the coach's public remarks bore no resemblance to their private discussion, marking the second time Jesus had broken his word. This prompted Ronaldo's decision to leave the training camp without waiting for further broken promises.

Coach Jesus, however, denied making any agreement with the player after Portugal's win over Norway, though he left the door open for Ronaldo's return. The Portuguese Football Federation has not yet commented on Ronaldo's statement.

Ronaldo apologized for not greeting supporters and for leaving his teammates, acknowledging that his captaincy made his conduct more serious. He accepts that the consequences of his actions must be assessed and punished by the FPF.

Despite the rupture, Ronaldo affirmed his international ambitions, stating he would be available to compete and win for the national team if physically fit and playing for his club after serving any imposed suspension.
